ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: (2010·Jiangsu) In space there is an electric field symmetrically distributed along the x-axis, and the graph of its electric field intensity E changing with x is shown in Figure 18-1 of the question. According to the graph, what is the relationship between the potentials at the two points x1 and -x1?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The potentials at the two points x1 and -x1 are equal
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: The attached figure is a graph of the electric field intensity E changing with the coordinate x, the vertical axis is labeled E, the horizontal axis is labeled x, and the origin is O. In the figure, positions such as x1, x2, x3, x4 are marked in the positive x direction; the curve represents the change of E with x, x1 corresponds to a point on the positive x side nearby, while the question requires comparing its potential with that of the -x1 point symmetric about the origin. Then reason: The stem states that the electric field is symmetrically distributed along the x-axis, so on the x-axis the x component of the electric field intensity is an odd function with respect to the origin, that is, E_x(-x)=-E_x(x). The potential difference between the two points satisfies φ(x1)-φ(-x1)=-∫_{-x1}^{x1} E_x dx. Since E_x is an odd function, the integral over the symmetric interval [-x1,x1] is 0, so φ(x1)-φ(-x1)=0. Therefore φ(x1)=φ(-x1).
